{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>Mutual Non-Disclosure </SPAN 0><SPAN 1>Agreement</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>THIS MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT is made on (insert date) 2012</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>Between</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>(A) Wollaston School whose address for notifications under this Agreement is at Irchester Road, Wollaston, Wellingborough, Northamptonshire, NN29 7PH and</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>(B) [ insert company name ] a company incorporated in [ ] (registered no. [ ]), and whose registered office is at [ ] and whose address for notifications under this Agreement is [ ] (“ “).</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>Whereas</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>Wollaston School and [ ] are respectively the owners of Confidential Information which they have agreed to disclose to each other for the Purpose on the terms and conditions set out in this Agreement.</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>The parties agree as follows:</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>1 Interpretation</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>In this Agreement:</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>Affiliate means any other entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control with either party;</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>Confidential Information means any information disclosed (whether before or after the date of this Agreement, in writing, verbally or otherwise and whether directly or indirectly) by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party or an Affiliate of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party in connection with the Purpose;</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>Disclosing Party means the party to this Agreement disclosing the Confidential Information;</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>Purpose means discussions and negotiations between the parties in relation to the supply of IT infrastructure and services and the associated tender exercise; and</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>Receiving Party means the party to this Agreement to whom the Confidential Information is disclosed.</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>A reference to a person includes a reference to a body corporate, association or partnership and includes that person's successors.</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>2 Undertakings</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>Each party undertakes to keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential including, without limitation, taking the measures set out in Clause 3. </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>In addition, each party undertakes not to use the other party's Confidential Information except for the Purpose, not to disclose, copy, reproduce or distribute the other party's Confidential Information to a third person and to use all reasonable efforts to prevent any such disclosure except as permitted under Clause 4 but in no event less than reasonable security measures and reasonable care.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>3 Maintaining confidentiality</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>Each party shall, in relation to the Confidential Information of the other party, exercise in relation to the Confidential Information no lesser security measures and degree of care than those which it applies to its own confidential information.</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>4 Disclosure of information</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>4.1 </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>Each party may disclose the Confidential Information of the other party in the following circumstances:</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>(a) with the prior written consent of the other party;</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>(b) to its employees, professional advisors, affiliates, consultants, shareholders, financiers and authorised representatives but only to the extent that disclosure is necessary for the purpose; or</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>(c) where disclosure is required by law, by a court of competent jurisdiction, by the rules of any stock exchange or by another appropriate regulatory body, provided that all reasonable steps to prevent such disclosure shall be taken, the disclosure shall be of the minimum amount required, and the Receiving Party consults the Disclosing Party first on the proposed form, timing, nature and purpose of the disclosure with as much prior notice as is practicable in the circumstances.</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>4.2 </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>The Receiving Party shall inform the Recipient of the terms of this Agreement and shall ensure that the Recipient complies with the terms of this Agreement as if the Recipient were a party to this Agreement.</SPAN 29>
<SPAN 30>4.3 </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>The Receiving Party shall at the request of the Disclosing Party and at its own expense take such reasonable steps as the Disclosing Party may require to enforce the obligations of the Recipient under Clause 4.2 including (where necessary) the institution of legal proceedings.</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>4.4 </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>For the purposes of Clause 4 Recipient means a person to whom any Confidential Information is disclosed pursuant to Clause 4.1(a) or 4.1(b).</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>5 Exceptions</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>5.1 </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>This Agreement does not apply to Confidential Information:</SPAN 36>
<SPAN 37>(a) to the extent it is or becomes generally available to the public other than through a breach of this Agreement;</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>(b) which the Receiving Party can show by its written or other records was in its lawful possession prior to receipt from the Disclosing Party and which had not previously been obtained from the Disclosing Party or another person under an obligation of confidence;</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39>(c) which subsequently comes into the possession of the Receiving Party from a third party who does not owe the Disclosing Party an obligation of confidence in relation to it; or</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>(d) which has been independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information.</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>6 </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>No grant of rights</SPAN 42>
<SPAN 43>6.1 </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>No right or licence is granted to either party in relation to the other party's Confidential Information except as expressly set out in this Agreement and the Disclosing Party shall retain all rights, title and interest to its Confidential Information.</SPAN 44>
<SPAN 45>6.2 Neither party accepts responsibility for or makes a representation or warranty, express or implied, with respect to the truth, accuracy, completeness or reasonableness of the Confidential Information (including the non-infringement of any patent, copyright or other right of a third party). </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>Neither party is liable to the other party or another person in respect of the Confidential Information or its use. </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>This Clause will not exclude any liability for, or remedy in respect of, fraudulent misrepresentation.</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>6.3 </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>Save as expressly set out in this Agreement, neither party shall owe any duty of care to the other party nor any other person.</SPAN 49>
<SPAN 50>7 Duration of obligations</SPAN 50>
<SPAN 51>The obligations and responsibilities of the parties shall survive the termination of this Agreement.</SPAN 51>
<SPAN 52>8 </SPAN 52><SPAN 53>Return or destruction of confidential information</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54>8.1 Each party undertakes within three business days of the receipt of a written request of the other party or on termination of this Agreement, at the option of the other party:</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>(a) to return to the other party all of the other party's Confidential Information and that part of all documents and other material in its possession, custody or control that bear or incorporate any part of the other party's Confidential Information; or</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>(b) to destroy by shredding or incineration all of the other party's Confidential Information and that part of all documents and other material in its possession, custody or control which bear or incorporate any part of the other party's Confidential Information and take reasonable steps to expunge all Confidential Information (and any copy that may have been made) from any computer, word processor or other device containing the Confidential Information. </SPAN 56><SPAN 57>Any destruction of Confidential Information will be certified in writing to the other party by an authorised officer supervising it.</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58>9 Announcements</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59>Neither party shall disclose the Purpose or the existence of this Agreement or reveal that discussions are taking place between the parties to another person without the prior written consent of the other party except to the extent that such disclosure is required by law, by a court of competent jurisdiction, by the rules of any stock exchange or by another appropriate regulatory body.</SPAN 59>
<SPAN 60>10 General</SPAN 60>
<SPAN 61>10.1 </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>A variation of this Agreement is valid only if it is in writing and signed by or on behalf of each of the parties.</SPAN 62>
<SPAN 63>10.2 </SPAN 63><SPAN 64>Any failure or delay in exercising a right or remedy provided by this Agreement or by law does not constitute a waiver of that or of other rights or remedies. </SPAN 64><SPAN 65>No single or partial exercise of a right or remedy provided by this Agreement or by law prevents a further exercise of the right or remedy or the exercise of another right or remedy.</SPAN 65>
<SPAN 66>10.3 </SPAN 66><SPAN 67>The rights and remedies contained in this Agreement are cumulative and not exclusive of rights or remedies provided by law.</SPAN 67>
<SPAN 68>10.4 </SPAN 68><SPAN 69>It is acknowledged that damages would not be an adequate remedy for a breach of this Agreement and each party is entitled to the remedy of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief for a threatened or actual breach of this Agreement. </SPAN 69><SPAN 70>Any claim for losses under this Agreement shall be restricted to direct loss only and shall not extend to indirect or consequential loss.</SPAN 70>
<SPAN 71>10.5 </SPAN 71><SPAN 72>If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, that provision shall (so far as it is invalid or unenforceable) be given no effect and shall be deemed not to be included in this Agreement, but without invalidating any of the remaining provisions.</SPAN 72>
<SPAN 73>10.6 Each party is acting in this matter as principal and not as an agent or broker for any other person or entity.</SPAN 73>
<SPAN 74>10.7 </SPAN 74><SPAN 75>This Agreement shall supersede all other confidentiality agreements between the parties relating to the same subject matter.</SPAN 75>
<SPAN 76>11 Notices</SPAN 76>
<SPAN 77>11.1 </SPAN 77><SPAN 78>A notice or other communication under or in connection with this Agreement shall be in writing, in English and shall be delivered personally or sent by fax, to the party due to receive the notice or communication at its address set out in this Agreement or another address as specified by that party by written notice to the other.</SPAN 78>
<SPAN 79>11.2 </SPAN 79><SPAN 80>In the absence of evidence of earlier receipt, any notice or other communication shall be deemed to have been duly given, if delivered personally, when left at the address referred to in Clause 0 and if sent by fax, on completion of its transmission.</SPAN 80>
<SPAN 81>12 Governing law and jurisdiction</SPAN 81>
<SPAN 82>The construction, validity and performance of this Agreement shall be governed by the laws of England and Wales and the parties hereby submit to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.</SPAN 82>
<SPAN 83>13 Third Party Rights</SPAN 83>
<SPAN 84>A person who is not a party to this Agreement shall have no right under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 to enforce any of its terms.</SPAN 84>
<SPAN 85>14 Counterparts</SPAN 85>
<SPAN 86>This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts each of which when executed and delivered is an original, but all the counterparts together constitute the same document.</SPAN 86>
<SPAN 87>Executed by the parties on the date first above written</SPAN 87>
<SPAN 88>SIGNED</SPAN 88>
<SPAN 89>by</SPAN 89>
<SPAN 90>for and on behalf of WOLLASTON SCHOOL</SPAN 90>
<SPAN 91>SIGNED</SPAN 91>
<SPAN 92>by</SPAN 92>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required when the agreement or protected evaluation ends.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its trigger. Termination, expiration, conclusion of an evaluation, a determination that development cannot proceed, or cessation of interest qualifies when that event itself activates the duty. A request-only duty does not qualify. Nor does a party's unilateral decision not to proceed unless the clause treats that decision as the operative conclusion of the protected process.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete return-or-destruction duty together with its end-event trigger. Do not omit a governing introduction, and do not substitute a request trigger or a retention clause for the required end-event link.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, the agreement itself, or the existence of dealings.
guidance.inspection: A prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions exist establishes the hypothesis. A prohibition on public announcements concerning the agreement or transaction also qualifies; definition text alone must be paired with an operative nondisclosure duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative prohibition and the protected fact, retaining any governing introduction needed to connect a listed fact to the prohibition.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the identification condition grammatically governs every covered disclosure mode. A single terminal condition may govern an enumeration of oral, written, and electronic modes; different procedures may also govern different modes. Do not treat nature- or circumstances-based coverage as identification.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete definition or all clauses needed to show that every disclosure mode is subject to identification by the disclosing party.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make a copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative operational route for making copies, such as copies necessary for an authorized purpose or acknowledged backup creation. guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language that affirmatively authorizes, requires, or acknowledges copy creation and its condition; access, disclosure, derivative-document coverage, consent qualifiers, and breach-remedy clauses are insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement prohibits copying confidential information and contains no affirmative operational copying route.
guidance.inspection: A direct copy ban, including a ban stated as applying without prior consent or approval, negates the benchmark permission hypothesis when the complete agreement does not otherwise authorize necessary copies, backups, or another copying circumstance. Do not convert the consent qualifier itself into affirmative permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify across the agreement that no affirmative operational-copy or backup route qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.

guidance.when: The confidential-information definition enumerates subject matter or data categories.
guidance.inspection: Find an expressly covered non-technical category, such as business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contact, or transaction information. Generic references to all information, documents, analyses, form, or derivatives do not alone prove non-technical coverage.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definition and at least one explicit non-technical category; include continuation text when the category list crosses fragments.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exclusion, reservation, or acknowledgment concerning independent development.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may develop information independently without using or accessing the protected information. Prior approval to disclose, lawful receipt, or another unrelated exception does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the independent-development clause with its governing exclusion or reservation language when needed to make its legal function complete.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses information obtained from an external source or later made available non-confidentially.
guidance.inspection: Require lawful receipt from a source other than the disclosing party or its representatives, with the source free of confidentiality restrictions, or a later non-confidential release that makes the information externally available. Independent development is different. Information supplied by a third-party vendor through the disclosing party is still disclosed through the protected channel and is not an acquisition permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the external-source or non-confidential-release item and its governing exclusion introduction, including the condition on the source's authority or confidentiality duty.

guidance.when: The definition or coverage clause addresses communication form.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether oral or verbal communication is expressly within confidential information, including language covering information irrespective of communication form or information disclosed in writing and also orally. Do not infer oral coverage merely from derivative notes or documents.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language linking oral, verbal, or form-independent communication to confidential-information coverage, with any necessary definition continuation.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts recruiting, hiring, employment contact, or solicitation involving personnel of the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Find a prohibition on soliciting, employing, hiring, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel. Proxy solicitation, transaction standstill language, and general contact restrictions are not personnel nonsolicitation unless tied to employment or hiring.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative employment-related prohibition and the covered personnel class; include duration, targeting limits, or recruiting exceptions when they qualify the prohibition.

guidance.when: The agreement states that duties continue beyond an end event or remain effective for a post-event period.
guidance.inspection: Verify that confidentiality, non-use, or another agreement obligation continues after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent end of the protected relationship. Continuation merely after return or destruction does not establish survival of agreement termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the continuing obligation and the termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or equivalent end event to which continuation is linked.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure or access to employees, internal staff, or a defined representative class.
guidance.inspection: Confirm an operative permission and that employees or internal staff belong to the permitted class. A definition naming employees is insufficient without a disclosure route; a permission to consultants, agents, or affiliates alone does not establish employee sharing.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the disclosure or access permission and, if the permission uses a defined class, the definition proving employees are included, plus material need-to-know or confidentiality conditions.

guidance.when: A clause permits or addresses disclosure compelled by law, regulation, court order, governmental demand, or legal process.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether that compelled-disclosure event requires notice, consultation, or equivalent advance communication to the disclosing party, subject to any legal-permission qualifier. A compelled-disclosure exception without a communication duty is insufficient, as is notice of an unauthorized disclosure after it occurs.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the compelled-disclosure trigger and the notice or consultation duty, including cross-referenced or list-introduction text needed to connect them.

guidance.when: The agreement affirmatively permits use of confidential information or defined residual information beyond a transaction-specific or otherwise stated agreement purpose.
guidance.inspection: A permission to use protected information for any purpose, or for the recipient's general internal business purposes without tying use to the agreement's stated purpose, negates an exclusive-purpose restriction. Merely allowing copying, disclosure, or conduct of a proposed relationship does not establish this contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the affirmative broad-use permission and any definition needed to show that it applies to confidential information or information retained from it.

guidance.when: The agreement states who may receive confidential information and the exception is limited to employees.
guidance.inspection: If disclosure is prohibited to everyone except qualifying employees, and the complete agreement supplies no permission for consultants, agents, advisers, or other non-employees, the agreement negates permission to share with third parties. A consent-based possibility alone is not an existing sharing permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the employee-only exception and the governing prohibition, and verify that no independent non-employee disclosure route qualifies it.
